transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Good to meet you too. 

I guess I came in because, well... I honestly just can't see this studio or my life getting back on track anymore. It just feels like no matter how hard I work, or... or what kind of payment plan they put in front of me, it's not going to make a difference. I just don't see a way out of this.
Are you having thoughts of killing yourself?

No, no I'm not. I... I know I said I don't see a way out, but I didn't mean it like that. I don't want to kill myself. I just... I don't know how to fix the mess I'm in with the shop. But no, I haven't had thoughts of doing anything to myself.
Do these feelings seem mainly caused by the problems with your studio?

I honestly don't know. The shop is definitely the biggest thing on my mind right now, with the money and everything. But I'm not sure if it's the only reason I feel this way. I just know it's what's right in front of me... I haven't really thought about if it's the main cause or not.
Aside from the problems with your studio, have you still been feeling down in other parts of your life?

Yeah, I think I have. Most days, I... I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling already sitting on me before I even get out of bed. It's just there. And even when I'm in the shop, surrounded by the wood I used to really love working with, it all just feels flat. I have to fight with myself not to just stand there staring into space instead of working.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I mean... like I was just saying about the wood. That was always my main thing, the thing I enjoyed most. Now it just feels like a chore. Outside of that, I don't really know. I haven't been doing much else lately to even test it out, so I haven't really noticed.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, gray mood most days?

Well, it's been a while now. I'd say it started right around the time I took on the mortgage for the studio. That was a little over two years ago... probably about two years and two months, if I had to guess. It's just been dragging on since then.
In the past two years, has there been any stretch of two months or longer when you were not feeling this heavy, gray mood?
No, I don't think so. It's pretty much been there every day. I definitely haven't had a break from it for two months... it's just been a constant weight since it started.
During this time, have there ever been at least two weeks when your depression got noticeably worse than your usual baseline?

No, I wouldn't say there was a specific time where it got suddenly worse for a couple of weeks. It's just been the same heavy feeling the whole time, really. Just... consistently bad, day in and day out, without any major dips or spikes that I can remember.
During this time, have you been feeling badly about yourself?

Yeah, I have. It's like... well, if I'm building something and a joint doesn't line up perfect, or if I miss a deadline for a bid, I don't just think I made a mistake. I go straight to thinking I'm a lousy carpenter. It just makes me feel like maybe I had no business trying to run my own studio in the first place.
Do you often feel hopeless?

Yeah, I do. Honestly, that's why I finally came in. I just... I can't see this studio, or really my life, getting back on track anymore. It doesn't seem to matter how hard I work or what kind of payment plan the bank puts in front of me. It just feels like a dead end.
Have you been feeling low on energy most days?

Yeah, pretty much every day. By midmorning, my arms already feel like I've been hauling lumber all day. Even after a full night in bed, I just... I can barely push through the basic stuff like measuring, cutting, or returning phone calls without feeling completely wiped out.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions?

No, I don't think so. I mean... my focus seems mostly fine. I can still read my tape measure and figure out how to plan out a build. Making decisions about the work isn't really the issue. It's just... like I said, finding the actual energy to do it.
Did your low mood begin only after you took on the mortgage for the studio?
Yeah, that's exactly when it started. This whole thing has been going on since I took on that studio mortgage... which was a little over two years ago. Probably about two years and two months now.
Since this low mood began, have the problems with the studio mortgage been ongoing the whole time?

I'm not really sure what you mean by problems. I mean... I haven't missed any payments or anything like that. It's just a regular mortgage. The pressure of having to pay it every month has been there the whole time, yeah, but... no, there haven't been any actual problems with the bank or anything, if that's what you mean.
